To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) LFMMI is an effective objective function for training neural acoustic models, (ii) LFMMI training can be done without any frame-level cross- entropy pre-training, (iii) the computation of the forwardbackward algorithm can be made feasible for LFMMI using a phone n- gram language model, and (iv) the computation can be further sped up by computing the forward-backward pass at a reduced frame rate.

the proposed method of using a phone n- gram LM and reduced output frame-rate for LFMMI training is a practical and effective method for training neural network acoustic models for LVCSR.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the lattice-free MMI objective function can be efficiently computed for neural network acoustic models and it provides significant performance gains over the cross-entropy and other sequence training objective functions.
LFMMI provides a very efficient and effective method of training acoustic models, and can be used to replace cross-entropy and other objective functions in the current state of the art ASR systems.
the LFMMI criterion can be used for sequence training of neural networks without the need for cross-entropy pretraining, which is computationally expensive.
